headline: AI Adoption Races Ahead of Its Evidence as Districts Tighten Guardrails
thesis: With ~9 in 10 education users already using AI, researchers say the evidence base is "nearly nonexistent" and big districts are hitting pause.
summary: Microsoft's new report finds roughly 9 in 10 students, educators and leaders have used AI for school, yet Inside Higher Ed reports independent research on its learning benefits is "almost nonexistent" and Brookings' task force concludes current risks outweigh benefits. Policy is tightening: New York and Los Angeles have paused student-facing AI, CoSN released new screen-time guidance, and THE Journal notes GPT-6 Astra's "Critical" cyber rating just as identity-security vendors expand recovery tooling. On the infrastructure side, Learning Commons opened a platform for state standards and proven teaching methods, and EdTech Digest highlights a graduate experience gap, with 77% saying employers expect too much experience.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · September 29, 2026 · Items were sourced via web-search indexing rather than live page fetches; sources with no dated news reuse recent evergreen items, and some THE Journal items link to its news list page.

themes.title: Skills and the Entry-Level Squeeze
themes.body: 77% of graduates say employers expect too much experience, even as cyber ranges, school-data career pathways and workplace-learning investment try to bridge the gap.

themes.title: Screen-Time and Student-AI Guardrails

themes.title: Student-Facing Tech, Broadly Defined
themes.body: Accessible classroom audio, VR STEM, and a new K-5 writing program point to product work centered on how students actually experience learning.
